messages:
monitoring-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: chi1 region - GPU compute pool 7/8 pods failed, aggregated serving capacity for models 'redwood-gen2' & 'open-llama' dropped to 0%. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/d/chi1-gpu

jia: Oncall Jia jumping in. Can people paste kube events and autoscaler logs?
maria: grabbing logs now. initial look shows mass node taints: 'gpu-fault' and 'kernel-oom'. kubectl snippet:
```
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
chi1-gpu-01   NotReady   gpu-fault,kernel-oom   2d
chi1-gpu-02   NotReady   gpu-fault,kernel-oom   2d
chi1-gpu-03   NotReady   gpu-fault,kernel-oom   2d
```
alex: we rolled nvidia-driver v535->v537 earlier today to chi1 canaries. could be driver regression. any driver crashlogs?
maria: yes saw dmesg: repeated 'NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:3a:00: GPU has fallen off the bus' and `oom-killer` evictions. attaching tail of /var/log/kern.log: `gpu_fault+panic`
sam: net team seeing intermittent control plane connectivity to chi1 kube-api from autoscaler: ~18% packet loss over last 10m. also BGP flaps reported at edge router.
jia: ok, likely combined kernel + network instability causing kube controlplane to mark nodes unhealthy and autoscaler/eviction churn. impact: hosted inference in chi1 degraded to 0 capacity.
lina: Product/CS heads up — starting customer comms for Dedicated customers in chi1. We'll flag SLA risk.
alex: immediate mitigations: 1) disable cluster autoscaler actions for chi1 (prevent scale actions that might evict running pods), 2) add temporary routing rule to shift traffic away from chi1 to sfo1/ord3, 3) set model fallback to quantized variants to reduce footprint. I can run 1 and 3 now.
maria: Rolling back driver on a single canary node might be risky while kernel unstable. Recommend stop new driver deployments and try a soft reboot cycle on one isolated rack to validate hardware vs driver.
sam: Network team, please hold BGP flaps, checking fabric. I'm opening a ticket with net-ops and will patch / route to avoid chi1 egress for control plane until stable.
jia: Assignments: maria -> hardware/drivers triage (canary rollback plan), alex -> autoscaler & routing policy (~apply emergency routing), sam -> network mitigation (BGP suppression + control plane reachability), lina -> customer comms. We'll follow RACI in incident runbook.
alex: Applied autoscaler suppression patch (disabled scaleDown/scaleUp for chi1) and flipped routing policy to shift 40% traffic to sfo1 and 60% to ord3. Confirming route update: `rdw-route set chi1 -> fallback(sfo1,ord3) weight=40:60`
monitoring-bot: Route update detected. Traffic shifted: chi1=0% in API frontends, sfo1=41%, ord3=59%. Healthcheck results: errors at ord3 briefly spiked to 5% during warm-up.
maria: On the canary node reboot, we saw the same GPU error on boot. HDD SMART ok. leaning towards driver/kernel regression + sudden power-cycle events in rack PDUs. opening hardware support case.
jia: Good catch. If drivers are failing at boot we should avoid full fleet reboots. Keep canary offline for postmortem.
lina: CS sent initial advisory to impacted customers. Template used: "We're aware of an outage in chi1 affecting inference capacity. Traffic has been shifted; teams are working on recovery. ETA update in 30 minutes."
alex: Temporary capacity workaround: spinning up additional preemptible GPU instances in sfo1 to handle burst—estimated cost delta ~ +$2.5k/hr. Need approval to scale until chi1 stabilizes.
jia: Approve emergency spend up to $10k/hr for next 3 hours. Finance pinged.
sam: network note: control-plane packet loss resolved after suppressing flaky BGP peer, API reachability stable from autoscaler host pool.
maria: hardware vendor scheduled on-site inspection for rack A3 in chi1. They've queued incident PR ticket: INC-CH1-224.
jia: Next steps: 1) continue traffic shift to fully drain chi1 (target 100% fallback in 10m), 2) keep autoscaler suppressed, 3) wait for vendor findings before any fleet driver rollbacks, 4) update customers at +30m. Owners noted above.
monitoring-bot: Update: traffic now 100% shifted off chi1. Serving error rate for affected models dropped from 74% -> 3% across fallback regions.
alex: marking this thread as active incident. Will create postmortem stub after stabilizing.
lina: +1 on postmortem and customer follow-up.
jia: Thanks all — keep updates short here. next status in 15m. :thumbsup:
